title: Variables & Types
description: Declarations, types, literals, and constants in C
theory:
## Variables in C

Locals are stack objects or pointers; strings are **`const char *`** literals. `printf` formatting must match the exercise’s expected stdout exactly.

exercises.title: Declare a binding
exercises.description: Declare `age` as `int` with value `25` and print it with `printf` (no trailing newline in the output).
hints: `printf("%d", age);` without `\n` if the expected output has no newline

exercises.title: Multiple bindings
exercises.description: Print exactly `C 1.85` (no newline): the word C, a space, then the literal digits `1.85` (avoid `%.f` locale quirks by printing the fractional part literally).
hints: `printf("%s 1.85", name);` keeps the decimal point stable across locales

exercises.title: Numeric cast
exercises.description: Set `int x = 100`, assign to `double y`, and print `y` so the output looks like `100` with no fractional part (no newline).

exercises.title: Printing default-like values
exercises.description: Print integer zero, floating zero (show as `0` without decimals), two spaces, then the literal word `false` — matching the layout `0 0  false` (no newline).

exercises.title: Constants
exercises.description: Use `#define` so `MAX_SCORE` is `100` and `MIN_SCORE` is `0`. Print both separated by a single space (no newline).

exercises.title: Grouped values
exercises.description: Bind `host` to `"localhost"`, `port` to `8080`, and represent `debug` as true (use an `int` 0/1 or `_Bool`). Print: `localhost 8080 true` with spaces (no newline). C prints the lowercase word `true`.
hints: `printf("%s %d %s", host, port, "true");` when debug is on

exercises.title: Swap with a temporary
exercises.description: Set `a` and `b` to `5` and `10`, swap using a third variable, then print `a` and `b` separated by a space (no newline).
hints: `int t = a; a = b; b = t;`
